experiment: E9-promptcache-sweep: token-mix sweep of the MODELED priced comparison (completion-dominated vs input-dominated x 3 skew, mock, Section 5.7.1 method)

method.basis: Section 5.7.1 priced comparison (docs/AgentISA.md, 'A priced comparison') and the Appendix G protocol (docs/AgentISA_supplementary.md): the same three pricing modes, the same default prices ($3/M input, $15/M output), the same 0.1x prompt-cache read discount

modes.no_opt: every draw re-queries at full price
modes.agentisa_cache: only first occurrences are paid (the measured behavior of the Section 5.7.1 arms)
modes.provider_prompt_cache: MODELED: every draw queries; repeat prompts bill input tokens as prompt-cache reads at cache_read_rate x the input price; completions always bill at full price

method.labels: ALL cost, saving, gap, and ratio numbers in this document are MODELED-on-measured: prompt tokens are template-size accounted measurements (chars/4) of the exact prompt texts; the L* completion lengths are MODELED constants; prices are parameterized list-price stand-ins.  No dollar-savings claim is made.
method.token_mix_axis: completion tokens per call: 'mock_measured' uses the mock's template-accounted replies (the published mock paper-scale anchor); 'L<n>' models the alias's observed reply-binds-at-max_tokens behavior as a constant n tokens per call (L64 = the Section 5.7 ceiling, L512 = the Section 5.7.1 ceiling).  The grid spans the input-dominated extreme through the completion-dominated regime; realized mixes are in each cell's mix_coordinates
method.simplifications: inherits the overlay's documented simplifications: no 1.25x cache-write premium and no 1024-token minimum cacheable prefix (both favor the provider-cache baseline); list prices are stand-ins because the gateway's actual pricing is unknown
method.workload: the Section 5.7.1 seven-step service-log triage shape: one cacheable LLM-type step (classify_signature), one call per distinct incident-signature batch; seeded truncated-Zipf draws over the fixed 40-task universe

dependency.usage: compute_cost/COST_MODES (the Section 5.7.1 MODELED pricing overlay) plus the workload primitives (task_corpus, incident_signatures, cache_key_id, zipf_draws, CLASSIFY_PROMPT, the mock reply, and the chars/4 token accounting) -- imported, never copied

provenance.determinism: pure offline arithmetic over the seeded workload; identical (seeds, draws, population, mix grid, prices) reproduce identical data (the timestamp and git rev live in this provenance block only)

limitations: mock only: no live gateway, no gateway-reported tokens in this sweep (the published real-gateway anchor is quoted from its artifact for context)

the swept L* completion lengths are MODELED constants (the alias's observed reply-binds-at-max_tokens behavior), not generated text; classification semantics are out of scope, as in the published protocol
single workload shape: the Section 5.7.1 seven-step triage stream with one cacheable LLM-type step
the overlay's documented simplifications stand: no 1.25x cache-write premium and no 1024-token minimum cacheable prefix (both favor the provider-cache baseline)
GPTCache / approximate caching explicitly out of scope; no external-cache head-to-head is claimed

ordering_invariance.note: Under the Section 5.7.1 overlay the cost ordering agentisa_cache <= provider_prompt_cache <= no_opt is invariant across the entire swept grid: the result cache removes whole calls (repeat completions included) while the prompt-cache discount never touches completions.  The 'ranking is a function of the token mix' claim is therefore about the MARGIN (how close the provider prompt cache comes to the result cache), quantified by the crossovers below.
ordering_invariance.label: MODELED

ratio_0_5.definition: completion tokens per call at which the provider prompt cache's modeled saving equals half the result cache's (ratio crosses 0.5)

provider_saving_5pct.definition: completion tokens per call beyond which the provider prompt cache's modeled saving is below 5.0%

output_cost_share_50pct.definition: completion tokens per call at which completions reach half the no-optimization modeled cost (the cost-parity token-mix boundary)

ratio_0_5.definition: completion tokens per call at which the provider prompt cache's modeled saving equals half the result cache's (ratio crosses 0.5)

mock_paper_scale.role: the published mock paper-scale anchor (200 tasks x 1 seed x 3 Zipf levels); this sweep's seed-1000 'mock_measured' cells must reproduce its three pricing modes exactly

real_gateway_run.role: the published completion-dominated anchor (real gateway, s=1.0, 50 realizations, max_tokens=512); its numbers are quoted from the artifact, not recomputed
real_gateway_run.label: MODELED-on-measured (published)

real_mix_analog.note: the sweep's L512 point sits at the Section 5.7.1 real-gateway run's max_tokens level; compare its mix coordinates with published_anchor_checks.real_gateway_run.mix_coordinates

the ordinal cost ranking of the two caching strategies is invariant under this overlay (see analysis.ordering_invariance); what the token mix changes is the margin, quantified by the per-skew crossovers
